geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a split-wing condition to break the sealed bar, create a legible entry seam, and better align the lower mass with the required active street threshold.
Keep the split legible along the long axis of the bar so the resulting void reads as a continuous public cut rather than a random fracture.
Open a modest gap to strengthen the entry/court figure without fragmenting the primary mass.
Preserve a grounded base connection so the split-wing gesture still reads as one neighborhood building rather than two detached pieces.
Keep the ground spine substantial enough to read as active occupied base, not just structural residue.
Lower the spine height so the public opening feels usable and grounded at pedestrian scale.

graph_edits.rationale: Swap the pure cantilever ending for a split-wing/public-threshold response so the access edge can register as a clearer ground opening rather than a sealed bar end.
Bring the dominant overhang earlier so more of the mass can lift off a grounded entry zone and strengthen the public threshold.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent-and-cantilevered bar with a clear main mass and decent repair integrity across views. It is not view-dependent or self-colliding, and the parcel containment appears coherent. The main weakness is programmatic/public-edge clarity: the verified access edge does not produce a strong enough ground void, entry seam, or courtyard-like public threshold, so the mass feels more like a compact sculpted block than a neighborhood-active street building. The silhouette is acceptable as an early stepped/bent landform, but the section does not yet convincingly express an active lower public zone and calmer upper hierarchy. Overall it is plausible for neighborhood living, but only moderately aligned with the required active ground condition.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stacked massing with a clear base-to-top hierarchy and compact urban scale can support mixed-use neighborhood living.
